reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read Matthew's shut-door command as targeting ostentatious motive, not publicity itself, fitting Jesus's tomb-side prayer and Paul's every-place command.

sides.snippet: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner chamber, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret
sides.verseText: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner chamber, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

sides.snippet: I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without wrath and doubting.
sides.verseText: I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without wrath and doubting.
